Subject: Dedicated pool questions + billing split for prod/dev

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to get a clearer picture of how Redwood would size a dedicated GPU pool for our workload and how billing can be split across two SLAs (Production / Developer). A few details from our side:
- Expected steady request volume: ~120k requests/day (text generation + embeddings).
- Typical context length: 800-1200 tokens; ~10% of calls are long (2k+).
- Peak concurrency observed during batch windows: ~480 concurrent inference sessions; typical working-hours concurrency: ~180.
- Latency target for production routes: 95th <= 250ms (for 512-token responses).

Questions:
1) Recommended GPU pool size (GPU type & count) for the baseline (no autoscale) to meet those targets with a 99% availability SLA?
2) How would burst capacity be handled and priced if we want a split billing model — prod pays for reserved baseline and dev is billed either pay-as-you-go or lower-priority burst?
3) What commit terms give us the most predictable unit costs (6 vs 12 vs 24 months) and typical discount bands for committed baseline capacity?

I've attached a small workload summary (horizon_workload_summary.xlsx). Procurement would like a short proposal we can attach to an internal purchase request.

Best,
Lisa Park
Head of Platform Engineering
Horizon Biotech

Lisa — thanks for the clear summary and the attachment. Quick answers up front; details below.

Short recommendation (baseline):
- Pool: 6 x 80GB GPUs (or equivalent A100-80GB instances; we can map to A10G alternatives for cost-sensitive options).
- Baseline throughput: ~1,200 tokens/sec per 80GB GPU for mixed gen/embedding workload (with smart batching + KV cache). This maps to an estimated steady-state capacity to cover 120k requests/day with your concurrency profile and 10% long calls while meeting 95th/99th latency targets.
- Burst: configure burst non-guaranteed capacity up to +50% via autoscale (pay-as-you-go hourly) and a prioritized routing policy so production traffic keeps baseline priority.

Pricing & commits:
- 6-month reserve: recommended if you want flexibility; typical list discount ~10% off on-demand baseline unit price.
- 12-month reserve: recommend for unit-price predictability; typical discount ~15% and better access to burst credit pooling.
- 24-month reserve: deeper discounts possible (~20%+) but requires procurement signoff.

Split billing model options (recommended):
A) Dual-account split: create two routes in Redwood (prod/dev). Prod is covered by the reserved baseline (6 GPUs); dev traffic billed to pay-as-you-go with a lower SLA. Monthly invoice shows the reserved baseline charge on the deal and separate usage line for dev-burst.
B) Shared baseline + internal reallocation: reserve the full baseline and apply internal tagging to bill specific routes proportionally (useful if Horizon wants a single PO).

Next steps: I'll pull together a committed pricing worksheet and a short SLA summary for your procurement team. Any preference on commit term?

-Jasmine
